additions.reason: Line 16: 'הַדִּבּוּר נִקְרָא אַמָּה'. The Rebbe explicitly uses נִקְרָא (is called) language — the formal bechina marker — to equate דיבור (speech) with אמה (cubit). concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 41: 'הַיְרִידָה וְהַנְּפִילָה שֶׁל זֶה הוּא בְּחִינַת עֲלִיָּה שֶׁל זֶה'. This IS a bechina statement, but it is a relative/contextual equivalence — the falling-of-one person equals the rising-of-another person. This is a dynamic teaching (from the question-and-answer section about exiting through the fallen openings of a friend) and the 'bechina' is explicitly qualified by 'לְגַבֵּי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ הַשְּׁפָלָה' — relative to his low level. This is better classified as an eitza (explanation of how rising works through another's fall) than a symmetric bechina of shared nature. Excluded per framework strictness.
